title: Customer maturity roadmap workshop — 90m facilitator canvas
content:
Purpose and where to use this canvas:

This doc is a compact facilitator canvas for a 90-minute customer maturity roadmap workshop — a focused session to: align stakeholders on current adoption maturity, surface strategic gaps tied to renewal risk, and convert the conversation into a concrete 90-day commitment plan. It’s intentionally short-form (90 minutes) to be used as a pre-QBR, renewal prep workshop, or as a focused add-on for mid-market accounts.

High-level objectives (pick 2–3 before the session):
- Shared diagnosis: get customer & CS aligned on 3 core maturity domains and their current maturity levels.
- Prioritized outcomes: identify 1–2 high-impact initiatives that materially affect renewal or expansion.
- Clear commitments: owner + first deliverable + date for each initiative.

When to run this: 6–10 weeks before renewal or after a major prod rollout or outage that changed adoption signals.

Pre-work (send 7 days prior):
- 1-page context brief (one slide): account snapshot, renewal window, recent usage trends (top 3 signals), known blockers.
- Short maturity survey (3 questions per domain) for stakeholders; send via Google Form to collect quick scores.
- Invite list: customer PM, engineering liaison (if available), two exec/stakeholder seats, account exec, CS lead, solutions engineer.
- Prep note for facilitator: one-line hypothesis for each domain (e.g., "onboarding friction causing stalled workflows").

Materials to bring to session:
- Shared Miro/Google Jamboard template (maturity axes + commitment sticky notes)
- Account health dashboard link and 2 quick charts (DAU for core feature, 30d token spend, conversion metric)
- One-pager renewal threshold note (if there are contract KPIs)

Agenda (90 minutes) — timeboxed:
1) 0–8m: Kickoff + objectives (facilitator)
- Quick introductions (name + 1-line priority) — keep to 30s per person
- State three working outcomes explicitly (diagnosis, priority, commitments)
- Social contract: candidness, timebox, one conversation at a time

2) 8–28m: Rapid evidence review (20m)
- Facilitator: 7-slide max snapshot (usage trend, top success stories, top support tickets, recent NPS/CSAT points)
- Customer: 2 min to add context or correct any data
- Goal: align on one signal that is most important for renewal (facilitator to write on board)

3) 28–58m: Maturity mapping (30m) — 3 lanes, 10 minutes each
- Domains (example set — pick 3 that fit account): Adoption & Usage, Implementation & Integration, Biz Outcome Measurement
- For each domain: quick definition (30s), customer rates current maturity (low/medium/high) using thumbs or survey data (90s), then 6 minutes of discussion to surface root cause and one opportunity
- Facilitator captures current level + one sentence root cause + tangent notes on board

4) 58–75m: Prioritization grid + decision (17m)
- Rapid vote: each participant gets 3 votes on the sticky notes representing opportunities
- Rank by impact vs effort on a 2x2 (high/low) on the shared board (10m)
- Facilitator calls for the top 1–2 to move forward as candidate commitments (7m)

5) 75–88m: Commitment drafting (13m)
- For each selected initiative, fill the commitment card: title; owner (customer and CS); first deliverable (clear, measurable); due date (<=90 days); success metric; knock-on dependencies. Use template below.
- Quick RACI shorthand: who informs, who approves, who executes.

6) 88–90m: Close + next steps (2m)
- Confirm follow-up cadence (weekly digest or biweekly checkpoint in CS cadence)
- Assign note taker to export board and drop into account Confluence + link to AE pipeline notes

Commitment card template (use as sticky note fields):
- Title: short
- Owner (customer): name + role
- CS partner (owner): name
- First deliverable: concrete artifact/step ("deploy integration v1" / "deliver admin training 2h")
- Due date: yyyy-mm-dd
- Success metric: numeric or binary ("reduce support tickets for X by 40%", "10 active seats")
- Risks/dependencies: short list

Facilitator script (snippets to read aloud or paraphrase):
- Kickoff: "Thanks everyone — we’ll use this 90m to quickly align on the highest-leverage things that move renewal risk. I’ll timebox discussion and pull decisions into concrete next steps."
- Evidence review framing: "I’m not here to defend numbers; we want your POV. If anything here looks off, call it out and we’ll correct it in the notes."
- Maturity nudge: "Think of maturity as outcome capability, not feature presence. A customer can have a feature but low maturity if it's not driving outcomes."
- Prioritization call: "We’ll prioritize by impact on business outcomes and feasibility within the next 90 days. Vote honestly — we’ll use the votes to decide."
- Commitment close: "This is the contract between the customer team and our CS/SE team — a short, testable first step. If owner is unclear, we postpone to avoid rework."

Parking lot (to capture off-topic asks):
- Use a side column on the board for items that are important but not in-scope for this 90m. Tag with "PLANNED" or "BACKLOG" and owner to follow up asynchronously.

Templates / quick heuristics for common domains:
- Adoption & Usage: look for 3 signals — active seats, repeat task completion, feature depth (fraction of advanced feature users). Heuristic thresholds: low < 10% adoption, medium 10–40%, high > 40%
- Implementation & Integration: signals — number of open integration tickets, API success rate, time to first event. Low maturity: >6 open critical tickets or >30 days to first working event.
- Biz Outcome Measurement: signals — clear metric tied to business (e.g., "30% reduction in time to close"). Low maturity = no agreed success metric or no measurement pipeline.

Common traps and facilitator prompts (notes-to-self):
- Trap: session drifts to feature requests. Prompt: "That’s valuable; does that directly change the renewal signal? If not, park it."
- Trap: one stakeholder dominates. Prompt: "Let’s give space to others — we’ll go around for a quick input."
- Trap: action items without owners. Prompt: "Who will do the first concrete step by the due date? If no owner, we don’t move it forward."

Post-work outputs (within 48 hours):
- Export board snapshot + populate Confluence account page with: maturity snapshot, top 2 commitments, owners, dates, and a one-paragraph executive note for AE to use in renewal convo.
- Create follow-up Jira/Asana tasks for each commitment with due dates and owners (link to tickets in notes).
- Short email template (to send to stakeholders) — copy/paste: "Thanks — great sync. Attached are the two commitments we agreed on and their owners. Next checkpoint: [date]. Please flag if any owner is incorrect."

Minimal measurement plan (for the 90-day horizon):
- Weekly: CS pulls 1-line status into AE digest (red/amber/green + short blocker)
- Every 30 days: update the success metric and share a 1-slide progress snapshot in account health deck
- If metrics go red: trigger a 15m rapid sync with customer exec + CS lead to re-plan

Variants (how to tailor the 90m):
- Executive-only (30–45m): cut evidence review to 5 minutes each; present 1–2 high-level tradeoffs and ask execs to choose; convert to 2 commitments.
- Technical deep-dive (120m): expand implementation lane to 40 minutes and invite SEs; capture detailed integration plan as deliverable.

Notes / TODO for facilitator (personal checklist):
- Confirm invite list 1 week out and ensure at least one exec is attending
- Send pre-work maturity survey and close responses 48h before session
- Create 1-slide data snapshot + share in calendar invite
- Prepare board template and commitment cards ahead of time

Appendix: quick example (realistic sketch)
Account: Acme Logistics — renewal 2026-01-12
- Pre-survey: Adoption 2/5, Integration 1/5, Biz measurement 2/5
- Evidence: usage trending flat; 3 open integration tickets; CSM hears exec worried about cost justification
- Top opportunities surfaced: 1) Integration quick-win (ETL connector for ERP), 2) Training for power users to unlock advanced features
- Votes: Integration 5, Training 3 => chosen initiatives
- Commitments: 
  - Integration quick-win: Owner (Customer) = Sarah M, CS = Diego R, Deliverable = prototype ETL connector installed in staging, Due = 2025-12-10, Success = staging pipeline passes smoke tests and 10 sample events flow
  - Training: Owner (Customer) = PM lead, CS = Maya C, Deliverable = 2-hour train-the-trainer session + 10 user sign-ups, Due = 2025-12-20, Success = 10 active users within 30 days

This canvas is intentionally prescriptive but light-touch — the goal is to leave with testable steps and a shared sense of whether renewal is on-track. Save this doc as "[account]-maturity-90d-canvas-v1" and attach the exported board to the account Confluence page.

End of document — facilitator notes: keep versioning simple (v1, v2), capture one metric per commitment, and always surface owners in the session to ensure accountability.
